questions.def: Regret + gerund describes regretting something you did.
questions.question: I regret ___ him the truth. He's very upset.

questions.def: Decide is followed by the infinitive form of the verb.
questions.question: She decided ___ abroad next year.

questions.def: Go is followed by the gerund for activities: 'go shopping'.
questions.question: Having finished my work, I went to shopping.

questions.def: Enjoy is followed by the gerund form of the verb.
questions.question: She enjoys ___ novels in her free time.

questions.def: 'Be used to' + gerund means accustomed to something.
questions.question: He is used ___ early every morning.

questions.def: 'It's no use' is followed by the gerund.
questions.question: It's no use ___ about it now.

questions.def: Look forward to is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.
questions.question: I'm looking forward to see you next week.

questions.def: Postpone is followed by the gerund form of the verb.
questions.question: He postponed ___ his family due to work.

questions.def: The subject position can be filled by a gerund phrase.
questions.question: ___ is believing.

questions.def: Advise someone is followed by 'to' + infinitive.
questions.question: I advised him ___ a doctor.

questions.def: The verb 'avoid' requires a gerund, not an infinitive.
questions.question: She avoids to go out alone at night.

questions.def: Fond of is a prepositional phrase followed by a gerund.
questions.question: She is fond of ___ in the ocean.

questions.def: Start can be followed by either a gerund or infinitive.
questions.question: The baby started ___.

questions.def: Stop + infinitive means stopping to do something.
questions.question: I stopped ___ some milk on the way home.

questions.def: After 'for' + object pronoun, use 'to understand'.
questions.question: It is difficult for him understanding the lecture.

questions.def: Give up is followed by the gerund form of the verb.
questions.question: He gave up ___ last year.

questions.def: 'Can't help' is followed by the gerund.
questions.question: I can't help ___ when I see her.

questions.def: 'Need' is often followed by the infinitive.
questions.question: He needs ___ harder if he wants to pass.

questions.def: 'Planning on' is followed by a gerund.
questions.question: She is planning on go to Italy next summer.

questions.def: Mention is followed by the gerund.
questions.question: He mentioned ___ on a new project.

questions.def: It is + adjective is followed by 'to be'.
questions.question: It's important ___ on time.

questions.def: Purpose + 'to be' is followed by 'to' + infinitive.
questions.question: The purpose of the meeting is ___ the budget.

questions.def: 'Interested' is followed by 'in learning'.
questions.question: I am interested to learn more about the topic.

questions.def: 'No point in' is followed by a gerund.
questions.question: There's no point ___ that now.

questions.def: Consider is followed by the gerund.
questions.question: He is considering ___ a new car.

questions.def: Fail is followed by the infinitive.
questions.question: They failed ___ the exam.

questions.def: Pretend is followed by 'to' + infinitive.
questions.question: She pretended not knowing the answer to the question.

questions.def: Offer is usually followed by 'to' + infinitive.
questions.question: She offered ___ me with the dishes.

questions.def: Keep is followed by the gerund.
questions.question: She keeps ___ me the same questions.

questions.def: Remember + gerund means remembering a past event.
questions.question: I remember ___ him last year.
